paperTitle: LABORAL: A Transformational Game for Hand Stretching Exercises to Prevent Occupational Diseases
centralContribution: This work presents LABORAL, a transformational game designed to facilitate hand stretching exercises using gesture-interactions, aiming to prevent occupational diseases such as Repetitive Strain Injury (RSI) and Work-Related Musculoskeletal Disorder (WMSD) in individuals, particularly IT professionals, who perform repetitive movements using computers. The game was developed in Unity using the Leap Motion sensor to provide an engaging and educational platform for promoting upper limb health and behavioral transformation.

elements.name: Table I: Hand Physiotherapy Poses
elements.description: A table enumerating the 17 specific hand physiotherapy poses that players must imitate in the LABORAL game, which are central to the game's exercise mechanics.
elements.justification: This table lists the core content (the poses) around which the entire game is built and its interactions revolve, making it fundamental to understanding the game's purpose.

elements.name: Figure 1: Pose Imitation
elements.description: A figure illustrating the player imitating a hand physiotherapy pose over the Leap Motion sensor, which is the core interaction mechanism of LABORAL.
elements.justification: This image visually represents the fundamental interaction loop of the game, showing how users perform the exercises detailed in Table I using the Leap Motion sensor.

elements.name: Figures 2-6: Stretching Sequences
elements.description: A series of figures (Fig. 2-6) depicting the five fundamental stretching sequences (Tendinitis #1-3, Carpal Tunnel Syndrome, Epicondylitis) that group the hand physiotherapy poses for therapeutic routines.
elements.justification: These figures visualize the structured organization of the exercises within the game, illustrating how individual poses are combined into targeted prevention routines.

elements.name: Table II: Median Recognition Times
elements.description: A table presenting the median recognition times for the 17 isolated hand physiotherapy poses by the Leap Motion sensor during functional tests.
elements.justification: This table provides crucial quantitative data on the sensor's performance for individual poses, directly reflecting the technical feasibility and responsiveness of the game's core mechanic.
elements.groupingHint: Table III: Interruptions During Pose Maintenance

elements.name: Table III: Interruptions During Pose Maintenance
elements.description: A table detailing the number of interruptions encountered during the 10-second pose maintenance phase for various hand poses, indicating challenges in sustained recognition.
elements.justification: This table highlights specific poses that were difficult for the Leap Motion to maintain recognition for, providing insight into the system's limitations and performance bottlenecks.

elements.name: Table IV & V: Sequence Execution Results
elements.description: Tables (IV and V) summarizing the average execution times and failure counts for each of the five hand stretching sequences.
elements.justification: These tables present the aggregated performance results for the complete exercise routines, showing how the system performs under more realistic usage scenarios and identifying sequences with larger discrepancies from ideal times.
